questions.q: How does Darwin suggest we can better grasp natural selection?
a: By first studying how humans breed animals
By measuring the age of rocks
By comparing fossils with living plants
By tracking weather patterns over time
questions.why: Lesson 1 opens with human breeding of dogs and pigeons as a way to grasp how natural selection works.

questions.q: In the summary, natural selection is compared to what?
a: An invisible breeder selecting traits that aid survival
A clockmaker designing each species separately
A gardener watering every plant equally
A judge awarding prizes for beauty
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes nature as an invisible breeder that selects traits supporting survival rather than beauty.

questions.q: According to the summary, what mainly drives competition for mates?
a: Females choosing the traits they value in males
Males competing by hiding from females
Both sexes evolving identical displays
The environment selecting mates at random
questions.why: Lesson 2 notes that males adjust their traits to female preferences, giving females a say in how species evolve.

questions.q: Why does the summary say emus are found only in Australia?
a: Migration barriers like the surrounding ocean kept them there
They were outcompeted by larger birds on other continents
They evolved in Australia after the continents drifted apart
They cannot survive in any climate except a dry one
questions.why: Lesson 3 explains that migration barriers, such as the ocean around Australia, limit where species spread.

questions.q: How do some clams reach new habitats despite poor mobility?
a: They attach to ducks' feet and travel with them
They burrow through wet sand for miles
They ride ocean currents as larvae
They build shells that float on the surface
questions.why: Lesson 3 mentions clams that attach to ducks' feet to cross barriers their own mobility could not.
